title: Dependability Onramp: experiments, cadence, and ops backlog brief
content:
Purpose:
This brief lays out a compact, experiment-first onramp for cross-functional teams to converge on service-level objectives (SLOs), reduce ops debt, and seed an actionable backlog of reliability interventions. It prioritizes fast-feedback experiments over large one-shot projects so we can learn which guardrails and automations actually change customer experience and operational cost.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: core inference control plane, routing and model-serving surfaces, per-route latency and error signals, deploy pipelines that affect rollout safety.
- Not in scope for this onramp: billing models, long-term capacity procurement, legal/compliance audits (these will be handled in parallel tracks).
- Constraint: minimal infra changes allowed in first 6 weeks; reuse existing tracing/metrics/alerting where possible.

Objectives (90-day):
1) Produce uniform SLO definition templates for 3 canonical services (hosted API, routing, and KV cache) with owner sign-off.
2) Run 4 short (1–3 week) experiments that validate impact on key signals: p99 latency, user-facing error rate, and incident-to-MTTR.
3) Convert experiment outcomes into a prioritized ops backlog (10–15 actionable cards) with estimated effort and expected ROI.
4) Ship two lightweight automations (canary gating + alert routing playbook) to reduce human toil during rollouts.

Success metrics (how we know this worked):
- Signed SLO templates for 3 services (yes/no).
- At least 2 experiments show measurable improvement in target signal with clear causality.
- Backlog with >=10 prioritized items, 60% estimated as <5 engineer-days each.
- Canary gating prevents at least 1 customer-impacting rollout (tracked manually during 90 days).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Program lead: Evelyn Chen (SRE). Responsible for schedule, decisions, and stakeholder alignment.
- Engineering partners (service owners): Samir Gupta (Control Plane), Lena Ortiz (Routing), Markus Li (Model Serving).
- Product partner: Priya Desai (Product Ops) — prioritization & customer impact validation.
- Observability: Nora Patel — instrumentation and dashboarding support.
- Solutions/SE: Alex Park — customer-runbook sanity checks and canary scenarios.
- Exec sponsor: Head of Engineering (TBD) — monthly checkpoint and escalations.

Working assumptions:
- Teams will adopt the canonical SLO template but can customize thresholds; any deviation requires a short justification doc.
- Default measurement window will be 30d for steady-state calculations and 7d for short experiments.
- Errors counted are user-facing (4xx/5xx mapped through API gateway) unless service-owner requests alternate signal.

Experiment candidates (fast, falsifiable hypotheses):
1) Prefix KV cache warmup: hypothesis — pre-warming KV cache during scale events reduces p99 by 15% for cold-traffic flows. (Owner: Markus Li, 2w)
2) Adaptive batching thresholds: hypothesis — reducing max-batch-wait for interactive routes when concurrency >X reduces tail latency without increasing overall cost by >5%. (Owner: Lena Ortiz, 3w)
3) Canary traffic split + auto-rollback: hypothesis — automated canary gating with circuit-breaker will reduce incident-triggered rollbacks by 50%. (Owner: Samir Gupta, 3w)
4) Error-class routing for transient infra errors: hypothesis — routing retriable errors to a lower-cost fallback reduces customer-visible error-rate by 20% for transient infra blips. (Owner: Samir Gupta / Routing, 2w)

Each experiment plan must include: hypothesis, success criteria (quantitative), data dashboard, rollback plan, minimal infra changes, and postmortem template.

Experiment cadence and sprint plan (first 8 weeks):
- Week 0 (kickoff): Align stakeholders, finalize SLO template drafts, carve experiments.
- Weeks 1–2: Instrumentation spike + experiment 1 (KV warmup). Deliverable: dashboard + short findings doc.
- Weeks 3–4: Experiment 2 (adaptive batching) + update SLO drafts. Deliverable: performance comparison and config recommendations.
- Weeks 5–6: Experiment 3 (canary gating) + implement lightweight automation. Deliverable: gating policy + demo.
- Weeks 7–8: Experiment 4 (error-class routing) + synthesize backlog + prioritization workshop.
- Week 9+: Transition prioritized backlog into regular sprint planning; set weekly reliability standup.

Prioritization approach for ops backlog:
- Impact X Confidence / Effort (ICE-like) scoring. We will score each candidate and split into T-shirt buckets (small: <5d, medium: 5–15d, large: >15d).
- Preference for items that unlock automatic remediation or prevent escalations.

Deliverables (end of 90 days):
- SLO template pack (3 services) with examples and measurement queries.
- Experiment registry with outcomes (dashboard links, raw data pointers).
- Prioritized ops backlog (10–15 items) with owners and estimates.
- Two shipped automations: canary gating policy + alert-routing playbook.
- Postmortem/retro doc capturing lessons and next-phase recommendations.

Communication/meeting rhythm:
- Weekly 45m reliability standup (mon) — quick experiment status, blockers, and decisions.
- Biweekly stakeholder demo (every 2 weeks) — short demo of experiment results and decisions.
- Monthly exec readout (30m) — highlight wins, ask for resourcing/priority.
- Slack channel: #rel-onramp (use for async decisions and quick blockers).

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Instrumentation gaps prevent valid measurement. Mitigation: Reserve week 1–2 for instrumentation spike and skip experiment if gap >2d.
- Risk: Teams lack bandwidth. Mitigation: Decompose experiments into smaller slices and prioritize minimal viable checks. Consider SRE rotation support.
- Risk: Automation introduces regressions. Mitigation: require canary + staged rollout and maintain manual fallback.

Quick kickoff agenda (60m):
1) Introductions & outcomes wanted (5m)
2) Review scope and constraints (5m)
3) Confirm owners for 3 SLO templates (5m)
4) Present candidate experiments and rank top 4 (20m)
5) Instrumentation gaps and observability plan (10m)
6) Immediate next steps & meeting cadence (10m)

Immediate next steps (first 72 hours):
- Evelyn: schedule kickoff and create #rel-onramp channel.
- Samir, Lena, Markus: each pick the canonical service to own and draft a one-page SLO proposal.
- Nora (observability): run a short instrumentation audit and list missing metrics.
- Priya: gather top 3 customer-impact examples to validate SLO priorities.

Appendix: SLO template fields (quick):
- Service name (owner)
- User-facing KPI (e.g., request success rate, p99 tail latency)
- SLI definition and measurement window
- SLO target and rationale
- Burn rate policy and alerting thresholds
- Incident escalation steps and runbook link
- Review cadence and stakeholders

Notes and open questions:
- Do we standardize on 30d rolling windows or provide route-level flexibility? (open)
- How aggressive do we want automated fallback vs. preserving model fidelity? (product tradeoff)
- Should cost impact be a first-class factor in prioritization scoring? (recommend yes)

Contact and ownership: Evelyn Chen (evelyn.chen@redwood.com) — please ping for clarifying questions or to raise resourcing issues.

Document history: draft created 2026-02-15 by Evelyn Chen. Updates: 2026-03-04 incorporated instrumentation audit results and prioritized experiments list.
